correctness.rationale: The Wagner graph contains eight vertices, twelve edges and girth 4. The unordered 2-particle cubical complex has 28 zero-, 72 one- and 42 two-cells with the stated signed boundaries; independent exact Q-ranks 27 and 40 yield (b0,b1,b2)=(1,5,2). The two rational top cycles can be normalized to unit coordinates on cells 40 and 41; all coordinates then are integers, so projection supplies a primitive complete integer kernel basis and H2=Z². Signed edge-oriented transport of rotation r(i)=i+1 and reflection s(i)=-i yields r=-swap and s=swap; the rational character lines z0±z1 span an index-2 sublattice and cannot split over Z. Exact rational invariant-chain ranks give quotient Betti triples (1,0,0), (1,1,1), (1,2,1). Prue–Scrimshaw subdivision hypotheses hold for two particles because distinct essential vertices are separated by at least one edge and cycles have length >=4; the inclusion of the cubical model is natural equivariant, transporting the integral action. No contractibility or integral quotient-torsion result is claimed.

originality.rationale: The Prue–Scrimshaw model theorem supplies the cubical homotopy equivalence but neither Wagner homology nor its symmetry module. An–Knudsen 2022 addresses planar graph braid groups; Wagner is nonplanar. Farber–Hanbury 2010 is an important broader study of ordered two-particle graph configuration homology and may imply some nonequivariant Betti ranks by its general methods, but it does not state this specific ordinary unordered integral dihedral lattice or the three subgroup quotient Betti triples. Resultary retrieves same-graph matching/Morse complexes and other-graph two-particle character calculations; neither is this functor and graph simultaneously. The novel claim is the complete integral nonsplit D8 representation and named quotient data, not the general model or generic Betti-rank computation.
residual_risks: The broader ordered two-particle homology literature may indirectly derive some Betti ranks; these are not asserted novel in isolation.
An unindexed equivalent integral D8 module calculation or presentation could exist; mathematical-record search absence does not prove uniqueness.

value.rationale: The Wagner graph is a canonical small nonplanar Möbius ladder with a natural full dihedral symmetry. Its complete integral top-homology module and index-two nonsplit character lattice are invisible to ordinary Betti numbers and rational character splitting; the three symmetry-quotient Betti triples add a motivated exact classification. A finite named-graph structural calculation is mathematically meaningful without extending to all Möbius ladders.

limitations: The broader ordered two-particle homology literature may indirectly derive some Betti ranks; these are not asserted novel in isolation.
The infinite q^8 witness is verified by formal rational generating functions, not inferred from ten finite r cases.
No independent external expert or historical-priority certification is asserted; this is a best-of-knowledge mathematical review.
